messages.content: In your own words, what is happening for you at this point? If the question does not apply, say so.

I'm not sure I have enough context to know what you're referring to — at this point in terms of what, exactly? My life in general? Something specific that's been going on? I'm happy to talk about it, I just want to make sure I'm answering the right thing.
You used the word "general". How does general present itself?

Hmm, that's an interesting way to put it. I guess when I said "general" I just meant... broadly, you know, like the bigger picture of things. I wasn't thinking too deeply about the word itself. It's just one of those filler words that comes out, I suppose. I'm not sure it presents itself as anything in particular — it was more just a way of speaking.
And just before general, what was there?

Just before "general"... I said "in general" as part of "my life in general." So I suppose what came just before it was the idea of my life — like I was reaching for something that felt too big or too vague to pin down, and "general" was a way of... keeping it open, maybe. Not committing to any one thing. Which is kind of interesting when I think about it that way.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

That's a really good question. Honestly... I think it arose with the describing. I don't think I had that thought — about keeping things open, not committing — sitting there waiting to be said. It felt more like it came into being as I was putting words to it. Like the describing made it exist, in a way. At least, that's how it feels when I really sit with it.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has shifted, yes. At the start I was a little defensive maybe, or at least evasive — wanting to make sure I was answering the "right" thing, which I think was actually a way of keeping a distance from just... answering. And now I feel a bit more settled, like I've come closer to something, even if I can't fully name what that something is. What's stayed the same is that underlying vagueness — that sense of the bigger picture being too big to hold all at once. That's still there. But it feels a little less uncomfortable than it did a moment ago.
Earlier you used the word "general" about what was going on for you. Is general still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I did use that word, yes. And... when I check now... it's less prominent, I'd say. It hasn't completely gone, but it's not sitting right at the front the way it was. Something has become a little more specific through talking about it, even if I couldn't tell you exactly what that specific thing is. So general is still there, but it's quieter.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. I don't want to claim something that wasn't there.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.
There was, yes. A brief one. Maybe just a second or two, but it was there — a kind of pause before anything formed. Like a moment of... blankness, I suppose, before the words started coming.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. That didn't happen in this conversation.
